Integrated assessment with SLOOS overlay:
- Fed statement (Mar 15, 2020): Strongly cautious on near-term outlook as COVID-19 weighs on activity; inflation below 2%; energy sector under stress. Policy eased to the ELB (0–0.25%), large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repos, discount window cut, and coordinated USD swap lines to support market functioning and credit flow.
- SLOOS lens: Survey evidence points to tightening credit supply and weaker demand—banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development loans, tightened other terms across firm sizes, raised credit score thresholds and reduced credit limits; demand weakened notably in construction and some consumer categories (with some segments unchanged). Banks expected further tightening (especially for riskier loans), reduced risk tolerance, and deterioration in loan portfolios, collateral values, and HELOCs. These dynamics signal a contractionary credit channel that can blunt policy transmission and deepen the downturn.
- Net: Financial backstops and QE are meaningful mitigants, but SLOOS indicates bank lending standards tightening and anticipated deterioration, tilting overall sentiment more negative than a typical easing episode.
